title: Customer Success Engineer (Internship)
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.
Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.
To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.
BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.
Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.
Location
This is a six-month internship based at our HQ in central Zurich or in Munich. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely.
About the role
Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes - new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day.
This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. On the other you are on a call with a finance team explaining it and agreeing what to do. You need both, every day.
Our customers run their finance and supply chain processes on blp. When something does not behave the way they expected, a document that did not post, an exception that should have resolved itself, a number in a dashboard that looks wrong, they write to us. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next.
You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them.
The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now.
This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses.
How we think about ownership
You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. Knowing which situation you are in is part of the skill, and nobody will hold it against you for asking. What matters is that you are the face of blp to that customer, and that you take that seriously.
Most of our customers work in German and you will be in front of them from early on. That is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it is the best part of the job.
This is a real internship, not an observation post. You will be trusted with live customers quickly, with people close by while you learn.

title: Software Engineer, Search Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

The Search Product Infrastructure team builds the systems that power search experiences across ChatGPT. We partner with teams developing models, operating inference infrastructure, building specialized search experiences, and maintaining search indexes to bring advances in models and retrieval into production. Our work spans search orchestration, model serving, experimentation, and distributed systems, with direct impact on answer quality, responsiveness, reliability, and efficiency at ChatGPT scale.

About the Role

As a senior engineer on the Search Product Infrastructure team, you will design, build, and operate the systems that connect models with search at ChatGPT scale. You will tackle challenges in search orchestration, inference efficiency, experimentation, and production reliability, making tradeoffs that directly shape answer quality and user experience. Working closely with researchers and partner engineering teams, you will own projects from technical design through launch and iteration, evolving the architecture as models, product capabilities, and demand grow.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

- Design and evolve the services that coordinate search classification, retrieval, ranking, and model inference, working closely with researchers and partner engineering teams to bring new capabilities into production.

- Improve end-to-end latency, throughput, and infrastructure efficiency through profiling, caching, request routing, and capacity planning, making informed tradeoffs between search quality, reliability, and compute cost.

- Build experimentation tooling and automation to run reproducible A/B tests, define success metrics, and measure product impact. Use shadow traffic and load testing to validate system behavior, estimate capacity needs, and support safe production rollouts.

- Own production reliability through observability, resilient fallback behavior, incident response, and automation that improves launch safety and reduces operational toil.

- Build search APIs and tool interfaces that enable models and agents to retrieve information reliably while respecting access controls and preserving source attribution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have significant experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems, with depth in performance, reliability, or resource efficiency.

- Bring experience in one or more of search, information retrieval, ML infrastructure, inference serving, or other high-throughput online systems.

- Have strong programming and systems debugging skills, and are comfortable working across languages and unfamiliar parts of a production stack.

- Can turn ambiguous product or research needs into clear technical plans, align partners across teams, and carry projects through deployment and measurable results.

- Enjoy learning across systems and ML, investigating unfamiliar problems, and sharing technical decisions and lessons clearly with others.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Core Technology is the engineering backbone of Anduril's hardware platforms - the shared systems, components, and infrastructure that power products across every division. The team develops and sustains the critical electromechanical systems, drive systems, propulsion, actuation, and embedded electronics that make Anduril's autonomous systems work. 

About the Role

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own the planning, execution, and delivery of hardware development programs within Core Tech. You'll be the connective tissue between design engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, test, and operations - driving complex electromechanical products from concept through production. You'll work directly with engineering leads to build roadmaps, track milestones, manage risks, and make sure the right teams are engaged at the right time. Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) $70 K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth , we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

• 401K with maximum employee matching.

• Health care benefits.

• Full administrative support.

• Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.

• Customized schedules within available clinic hours.

• Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).

• Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.

• Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.

title: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking
description:
Position Summary
The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.
The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.
Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Risk Management

• Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.

• Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.

• Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.

• Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.

• Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

• Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:

• Mortgages

• Personal Loans

• Credit Cards

• Auto Loans

• Consumer Finance Products

• Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.

• Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.

• Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.

• Recommend risk-adjusted lending strategies.

Operational Risk Management

• Develop frameworks to identify and manage operational risks.

• Monitor operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks.

• Oversee business continuity and operational resilience programs.

• Strengthen internal controls and risk reporting mechanisms.

• Ensure effective risk and control self-assessment processes.

Regulatory Compliance & Conduct Risk

• Ensure compliance with banking regulations and consumer protection laws.

• Oversee conduct risk management and fair customer treatment initiatives.

• Maintain strong relationships with regulatory authorities.

• Lead regulatory examinations and risk-related audits.

• Ensure implementation of regulatory changes and risk controls.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk

• Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation programs.

• Strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing controls.

• Monitor financial crime risks and emerging threats.

• Ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.

• Collaborate with law enforcement and regulatory agencies when necessary.

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

• Monitor interest rate risk and liquidity risk exposures.

• Evaluate balance sheet vulnerabilities and stress scenarios.

• Support asset-liability management activities.

• Ensure adherence to regulatory capital and liquidity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

• Oversee technology and cyber risk governance.

• Assess cybersecurity threats and resilience capabilities.

• Ensure robust controls for digital banking platforms.

• Monitor third-party and vendor risk exposures.

• Support digital transformation initiatives through effective risk management.

Governance & Reporting

• Present risk reports to Executive Management, Risk Committees, and the Board.

• Develop key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk dashboards.

• Ensure timely escalation of significant risk issues.

• Maintain effective risk governance structures and committee frameworks.

Leadership & Talent Development

• Lead risk management teams across multiple disciplines.

• Develop future risk leaders and succession plans.

• Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and transparency.

• Promote collaboration across business, compliance, audit, and technology functions.

Qualifications
Education

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Risk Management, Mathematics, or a related discipline.

• Master's degree (MBA, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field) preferr

Stratejik planlama ile sahadaki birebir uygulamayı birbirine bağlayan; kritik, analitik odaklı ve liderlik vizyonu gerektiren bir pozisyondur.

Trendyol’da Sizi Neler Bekliyor?
- FlexBenefits: Günlük yemek bütçeni özelleştirebilir, sağlık sigortanı upgrade edebilir, akaryakıt desteği veya Trendyol alışveriş bakiyesi gibi ek haklar arasından ihtiyacına göre seçim yapabilirsin.
- İyi yaşam desteği: Lokasyon bazlı kurum içi doktorlarımızdan, psikolog ve diyetisyen desteğinden ve HPV aşısı kapsamından faydalanabilirsin.
- Kişiselleştirilmiş öğrenme ve gelişim fırsatları: Yıllık eğitim bütçeni ihtiyacana uygun olduğunu düşündüğün eğitim veya konferans için kullanabilirsin. LMS platformumuzdan dilediğin an faydalanabilir, yıl boyu sunulan yüz yüze eğitimlere katılabilirsin.
- İlk günden sorumluluk alma kültürü: Trendyol’da her ses duyulur ve değer görür. Sen de daha ilk günden itibaren inisiyatif alarak etki yaratabilirsin.
- Tek ruhlu, çok kültürlü bir ekip: Berlin’den Dubai’ye, Amsterdam’dan İstanbul’a... Farklı bakış açılarını bir araya getiren, start-up ruhuyla çalışan uluslararası bir ekibiz.
- En iyilerle birlikte gelişme imkânı: Anlamlı işlerde sorumluluk alabilir, deneyimleyerek öğrenebilirsin. Farklı ülkelerdeki ekip arkadaşlarımızdan mentorluk alabilir ve alanında uzman ekip arkadaşlarımızla birlikte kendini geliştirebilirsin.
- İş dışında da anlamlı bağlar: Ekip ritüelleri, etkinlikler ve sosyal aktiviteler sayesinde yalnızca birlikte çalışmıyor; birlikte gülüyor, öğreniyor ve ilham alıyoruz.

Bu rol seni heyecanlandırdıysa hemen başvur, bir sonraki adımı birlikte atalım.

The GSOC Manager will lead and operate Lila Sciences' Global Security Operations Center, owning the physical security technology stack and day-to-day security and intelligence operations for all sites globally. This role is responsible for enterprise access control management, Emergency Notification System (ENS) management, radio system management, visitor management, video surveillance, and intrusion detection systems, and acts as the central point of coordination for incident response and first-responder engagement. The GSOC Manager will build and maintain the SOPs, policies, and plans that govern GSOC operations, and will work in close, daily partnership with all Lila employees, the Senior Director - Protective Security, all facilities' security officers, Facilities, EHS, IT, contractors, building engineers, guests, and other third parties to keep Lila Sciences' people and sites safe and secure.

• Manage the enterprise access control system, including badge creation, access provisioning and deprovisioning, periodic access reviews, and compliance requirements.

• Monitor and manage the enterprise video surveillance system, including active surveillance, camera health, footage review, and retention practices.

• Monitor and manage the intrusion detection system (IDS) and associated alarms.

• Serve as the primary interface with police, fire, EMS, and other first responders during security or safety incidents.

• Monitor threat intelligence feeds and author threat intelligence reports and briefings for stakeholders.

• Track and monitor the locations and travel of executives and other traveling staff to support duty-of-care and travel-risk decisions.

• Partner closely with onsite security officers, Facilities, EHS, IT, contractors, building engineers, guests, and third parties to coordinate security activity across all sites.

• Bachelor's degree in security management, criminal justice, emergency management, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

• 5+ years (L5) to 8+ years (L6) of experience in corporate/physical security operations, a GSOC/SOC environment, law enforcement, or military service.

• Hands-on experience with access control systems and video management systems.

• Experience monitoring and managing intrusion detection/alarm systems.

• Demonstrated experience leading incident response coordination and interfacing with first responders.

• Experience ensuring compliance requirements (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2, NFPA, etc.).

• Experience managing Emergency Notification Systems and radio systems.

• Strong track record writing and maintaining SOPs, security policies, and emergency plans.

• Ability to work onsite full-time (40 hours/week) at 5 Alewife Park, Cambridge, MA.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with Facilities, EHS, IT, contractors, and building engineers.

• Professional demeanor and sound judgment when interfacing with executives, guests, and external stakeholders.

• Experience preparing and delivering written and verbal intelligence and incident briefings, presentations, and reports.

Bonus Points For

• Experience supporting life sciences, biotech, or R&D/lab environments.

title: Change Management Consultant – Banking & Wealth Transformation

About Capco

Capco is a global business and technology consultancy dedicated to the financial services industry. We combine deep industry expertise with consulting and transformation capabilities to help leading financial institutions navigate complex change and deliver meaningful outcomes.

Across APAC and globally, we partner with banks and financial institutions on programmes spanning business transformation, digital and technology change, operating model transformation, regulatory change and large-scale programme delivery.

As we continue to grow our Malaysia practice, we are looking for experienced change professionals who can help our clients successfully navigate transformation - ensuring stakeholders are engaged, impacted teams are prepared, and change is effectively embedded across the organisation.

Role Overview

We are looking for an experienced Change Management Consultant with a strong Banking and/or Wealth Management background to support complex transformation programmes across our financial services clients.

You will be responsible for understanding the people and organisational impacts of transformation and developing structured change approaches that enable successful adoption.

The role requires a strong combination of change management, stakeholder engagement and communications expertise, alongside sufficient banking domain knowledge to understand the business context in which change is taking place.

You will work closely with senior business stakeholders, programme leadership, technology and delivery teams to assess change impacts, identify stakeholder needs, develop communications and engagement strategies, and support the organisation through transition and implementation.

This is a hands-on, client-facing consulting role suited to someone who can navigate complex stakeholder environments, bring structure to change, and communicate effectively across different levels of an organisation.

Change Strategy & Planning

• Develop and execute change management strategies and plans aligned to programme objectives and business outcomes.

• Assess the scale, complexity and organisational impact of proposed changes.

• Define appropriate change interventions across different stakeholder and impacted-user groups.

• Develop integrated change plans covering stakeholder engagement, communications, readiness, adoption and implementation activities.

• Partner with programme leadership to ensure change considerations are embedded throughout the transformation lifecycle.

• Conduct change impact assessments to understand how transformation will affect people, processes, roles, systems and ways of working.

• Identify impacted stakeholder groups and assess the nature and significance of change across the organisation.

• Conduct readiness assessments and identify potential barriers to adoption.

• Develop appropriate mitigation and intervention plans to address identified change risks.

• Track change readiness and adoption throughout implementation.

Stakeholder Management & Engagement

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the PM for Growth at Factory, you’ll own our overall approach to get users active and productive on the platform.

You’ll be responsible for our activation metric: how do we measure what it means to be an activated user, and how do we get more users to that point and beyond, whether they’re coming from our self-serve product or onboarding via an enterprise deployment.

And you’ll own our self-serve product offering: what we provide as part of it, how we price and package it, the role it plays in our broader company strategy, and how we should evaluate its success.

There won’t be a single “growth” engineering team to work with-you’ll operate across multiple engineering pods and work closely with our Marketing, BizOps, and Deployment functions to make sure we’re doing the right things to create more happy Factory users.

You’ll need a strong thesis for what makes a compelling early software factory experience in a competitive market, and an opinion about how PLG best reinforces a top-down Enterprise motion. You’ll need sharp technical instincts, genuine empathy for developers, and the ability to make fast, high-quality decisions in ambiguity. You should be as comfortable diving into technical architecture discussions as you are presenting roadmap priorities to leadership.

Our goal with the product function at Factory is to be high-leverage, high-ownership, and hands-on-you can expect to be working directly with the C-suite at the largest companies in the world, and shipping improvements directly to the product. And you’ll be central to defining the role of Product in a software factory-driven organization-a pattern we intend to pioneer and then help distribute across our customer base and the broader industry.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

- Own the roadmap for multiple major areas of our product

- Partner closely with customers and work closely with data to understand pain points and translate them into product improvements.

- Work with engineering and research to ship features that keep Factory at the frontier of AI-powered development.

- Build frameworks and processes that scale as the product team grows.

- Actively engaged with the AI ecosystem, staying current on coding agents, model capabilities, and emerging industry trends through hands-on experimentation.Thrive in fast-moving, high-ambiguity environments and take ownership end-to-end.

The team works in the office 5 days a week in San Francisco (walking distance to Caltrain).

title: Principal Security Engineer Cloud and Infrastructure Security

Overview
Principal Security Engineer Cloud and Infrastructure Security
One Identity · Information Security, Attack Surface
Principal individual contributor · India · Reports to the Director of Information Security
Why this role exists
The architecture set in this role decides which certifications One Identity can hold and which markets we can sell into. That is unusual commercial weight for an engineering seat, and it comes with a mandate from leadership to build the program behind it.
We sell on-premises and hosted solutions. Some products run as hosted services we operate in Azure and AWS. Others ship as software customers deploy in their own datacenters. Infrastructure security here has two audiences: the environments we run, and the base images, container definitions, and deployment defaults we publish, which become part of every customer's environment. A hardening decision made once is inherited by everyone who deploys it.
We're separating from Quest Software and building an independent security function. The team is lean and globally distributed, and this role is its senior technical voice. Scope comes from what you design and automate, and from what engineering chooses to adopt.
What you'll do
Shape the architecture

• Own security architecture across Azure and AWS: tenant, subscription and account design, network segmentation and traffic control, private connectivity, egress policy, workload isolation. Where a regulated market or a certification constrains a design, you're expected to know before it's committed.

• Run our own products against real security requirements and tell us what you find. IT operates our privileged access controls on One Identity software, so you'll see how our products hold up under production pressure and take that back to the teams building them.

• Bring engineering into architectural decisions early. Designs teams help shape are the ones that hold up in production.

Raise the engineering bar

• Teams already build with infrastructure as code across both clouds. Raise the security ceiling inside that practice: hardened modules, secure-by-default landing zones and account baselines, and patterns teams reach for because they're better.

• Extend policy as code across the pipeline and the platform so teams get a signal at commit time.

• Own the hardened image pipeline for virtual machines and containers, covering the fleet we run and the images we publish: build, patch cadence, provenance, signing, and the automation that keeps both current.

• Set the security architecture for AI workloads: model and inference endpoint exposure, data boundaries and residency, identity for agents and service principals, secrets handling, and guardrails around AI tooling in the development lifecycle.

• Elevate cloud posture and workload protection into a single practice spanning Azure and AWS. You set the platform direction, the coverage standard both clouds are held to, and the path findings take to the teams that own them.

Where a person still has to act, the finding arrives with owner, fix path, and rationale. Where we can act ourselves, it arrives as a pull request against the module, image definition, or policy that produced it. PRs, not tickets.

Traditional IAM teams operate as an approval queue: a request comes in, someone reviews it, grants it, and (hopefully) remembers to revoke it. That model doesn't scale past a certain point, and Vercel is past it. Adding more approvers doesn't close the gap. Building the system that makes access self-serve, time-bound, and provable does.

This role is about building that system. Identity at Vercel should work like the rest of our infrastructure: defined as code, reviewed in pull requests, deployed through CI, and observable in production. Provisioning, deprovisioning, and access reviews become workflows the system runs, with the audit evidence for SOC 2 and similar generated as a byproduct rather than a manual scramble.

title: Product Craftsperson - I
description:
This is a remote position.
Experience Level
We're looking for a seasoned Product Owner with at least 2-4 years of experience owning a product backlog end-to-end within an Agile delivery environment. You should be a "delivery craftsperson" who can demonstrate a track record of turning ambiguous, cross-team requirements into shipped, working software - with particular comfort operating inside platforms where your product's success depends on coordination with teams you don't manage.
Role Overview
As a Product Owner, you will own the backlog and delivery cadence for one product within a tightly interconnected platform, where your product's roadmap depends on - and feeds into - several sibling products. You'll act as the point of alignment between engineering teams, supporting product managers, and client stakeholders, translating business and compliance needs into backlog items ready for a development team to execute against.
A key part of the role is holding the line on requirements quality: defining clear acceptance criteria before work enters a sprint, and sequencing competing demands - new features, maintenance of live services, and production support - that your team carries simultaneously. Because your product does not operate in isolation, a large part of the job is coordinating dependencies across teams that don't report to you.
Key Responsibilities

•
Backlog Ownership & Requirements Definition: Own and prioritize the product backlog; define acceptance criteria for accuracy, completeness, and readiness before stories are marked sprint-ready.

•
Cross-Team Dependency Coordination: Sequence and negotiate delivery across multiple dependent engineering teams (platform, integration, infrastructure, and adjacent product teams), since most features require multi-team scheduling rather than single-team execution.

•
Delivery Prioritization Under Competing Demands: Balance new feature development, maintenance of live production services, and active production support within the same backlog, without letting one silently starve the others.

•
Domain Ramp-Up: Build working depth in the specific technical and regulatory domain tied to your assigned product - this may include healthcare EDI transaction standards, web-automation/data-extraction reliability, credential and access-security models, or regulated payments and remittance processing, depending on placement.

•
Stakeholder & Requirements Governance: Partner with the supporting Product Manager and client-side stakeholders to close open requirement decisions before development starts, hold sign-off discipline, and manage rework risk from late-stage scope changes.

•
Data & Interface Quality Ownership: Where your product's output feeds downstream systems, own the interface contract (field definitions, data completeness, naming) to prevent avoidable rework further down the chain.

Requirements
What We're Looking For

•
Proven Product Ownership Experience: Track record owning a backlog end-to-end in an Agile environment, ideally within a platform where products are tightly coupled rather than independent.

•
Domain Adaptability: Comfort ramping quickly into unfamiliar technical or regulatory domains - some assignments require near-immediate fluency (e.g., regulated payments, EDI standards), while others allow for a longer runway.

•
Cross-Functional Coordination Skills: Demonstrated ability to sequence work and resolve competing priorities across multiple engineering teams that don't report into the same chain.

•
Analytical Rigor: Ability to write precise, testable acceptance criteria and reason through data quality or completeness gaps before they become delivery blockers.

•
Strong Stakeholder Communication: Comfortable representing product status and trade-offs to both engineering teams and client-facing stakeholders, in plain, non-technical language when needed.

The Director, Financial Reporting & Internal Controls is responsible for the Company’s consolidated financial reporting, technical accounting, global statutory reporting and audit activities, and oversight of the internal control environment. This role will oversee a small team, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, workload prioritization and performance support while ensuring high-quality execution of key reporting and control deliverables. The role partners closely with senior finance leadership, regional finance teams, cross-functional stakeholders and external auditors.

Key Responsibilities

• Prepare the Company’s quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements and related disclosures in accordance with IFRS.

• Support quarterly and annual reporting processes and review significant accounting entries and adjustments.

• Ensure consistency and accuracy of financial reporting across the organization.

• Lead the consolidated financial statement audit, acting as the primary relationship manager with external auditors, coordinating key deliverables, reviewing and participating in the negotiation of audit fees, and resolving audit and accounting matters.

• Serve as a key technical accounting resource and lead the assessment and documentation of complex and non-routine transactions under IFRS, including revenue recognition, share-based compensation, leases, pensions, restructuring and provisions, impairments, business combinations, legal entity restructuring and other complex accounting matters.

• Monitor new accounting standards and developments and assess their impact on the Company’s financial reporting and accounting policies.

• Oversee global statutory financial statements, audits and required filings across multiple jurisdictions, including managing the statutory audit calendar, coordinating with local finance teams, external auditors and service providers, monitoring progress and driving timely completion.

• Oversee the financial internal control environment, including monitoring key controls, identifying control gaps and supporting remediation activities.

• Partner with Tax, Treasury, Legal and other functions on significant transactions, restructurings and other accounting matters.

• Support acquisitions, integrations, legal entity restructurings and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and financial reporting perspective.

• Drive continuous improvement and standardization of financial reporting, statutory audit and related finance processes.

• Lead, coach and develop a small team, including setting priorities, assigning work, providing timely feedback and supporting professional growth.

• Promote a collaborative, high-performance team environment with clear expectations, effective communication and accountability for deliverables.

• Support ad hoc projects and transactions as required.

Requirements

• Must hold a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, ACA, or ACCA).

• 10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, preferably including experience in a large multinational organization and/or public accounting.

• Strong knowledge of IFRS.

• Experience in preparing consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.

• Strong technical accounting research and documentation skill

title: Import Compliance Manager
description:
JOB SUMMARY:
The Import Compliance Manager is responsible for ensuring the company's import operations comply with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations and all applicable trade laws. This role oversees the accurate classification of imported goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), manages relationships with customs brokers and freight forwarders, and coordinates the end-to-end flow of container shipments from origin to destination, including bonded warehouse operations and duty drawback recovery. The ideal candidate combines deep trade compliance expertise with hands-on experience managing container logistics and import documentation.
JOB DUTIES:

• Manage the classification of imported products under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), ensuring accuracy and consistency across the product catalog.

• Oversee end-to-end container import operations, including booking, customs clearance, port coordination, and delivery to distribution centers or warehouses.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customs brokers, freight forwarders, and carriers to resolve clearance delays, documentation discrepancies, and duty disputes.

• Ensure compliance with CBP regulations, Importer Security Filing (ISF) requirements, and other federal import/export regulations.

• Maintain and audit import records, entry summaries, and classification rulings to support recordkeeping requirements and prepare for CBP audits.

• Manage bonded warehouse operations, including inventory control, CBP-mandated recordkeeping, withdrawal entries, and coordination with warehouse operators to ensure compliance with 19 CFR Part 19.

• Monitor changes in tariff schedules, trade agreements, and duty rates (including Section 301, antidumping/countervailing duties) and assess their impact on the business.

• Identify and pursue duty savings opportunities, including free trade agreement eligibility, bonded warehouse deferral strategies, duty drawback, and first sale valuation.

• Administer the company's duty drawback program end-to-end: identify eligible import/export transactions, prepare and file drawback claims, maintain supporting documentation, and manage relationships with drawback service providers or brokers to maximize duty recovery.

• Partner with procurement, finance, and legal teams to evaluate landed cost impacts of tariff changes and sourcing decisions.

• Develop and maintain internal compliance policies, standard operating procedures, and training materials for classification and import processes.

• Manage and mentor import compliance analysts or coordinators, as applicable.

• Track key performance metrics related to container transit times, customs clearance rates, and compliance audit outcomes.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's degree in International Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or related field.

• 5+ years of experience in import compliance, customs brokerage, or international trade, with direct experience in HTS classification. Strong working knowledge of CBP regulations, Incoterms, and international shipping documentation (bills of lading, commercial invoices, certificates of origin).

• Experience managing container shipments and coordinating with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.

• Experience with bonded warehouse (Class 3) operations and duty drawback claim preparation and filing.

• Familiarity with trade compliance software and ERP/TMS systems (e.g., SAP GTS, Oracle GTM, Descartes).

• Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) credential preferred, not required.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and cross-functional communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple shipments and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

$90,000 to $120,000, DOE

title: Staff Engineer
description:
About AlphaSense: 

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

About the Team:

The User Management team owns the full identity lifecycle at AlphaSense - from creating and provisioning users, through managing their identities, to authenticating who they are and authorizing what they can do in the system. Our work spans three core domains:

• User Management - creating, provisioning, and managing user identities

• Authentication - verifying who users are

• Authorization - determining what users can do in the system

We are a product platform team, not a product team: we build the identity and access infrastructure that other engineering teams build on top of, rather than shipping user-facing features ourselves. We also act as a security guardrail for AlphaSense, since identity and access sit at the center of how the platform stays secure.

The team is well-established and senior, based in Helsinki, Finland. We're now expanding into North America - with roles based in both Canada and the US - to build follow-the-sun coverage, so our customers get proper support around the clock, and to push deliberately toward a true platform model - scaling our authentication and authorization systems so they can be safely self-served by teams across the company.

About the Role: 

This is a Staff Engineer role on the team that manages identity and access for AlphaSense's entire, and constantly growing, customer base, and that nearly every product engineering team depends on for user and entitlement data. You'll work across all three pillars of identity: creating and managing users, authenticating them, and authorizing what they can do - designing systems built to scale with a constantly growing number of users. title: Healthcare Project Manager
description:
ABOUT US
Verian Lithuania (formerly PPMI ) is a European policy research and evaluation consultancy. We work primarily for EU institutions (European Commission, JRC, DG SANTE, HaDEA, EUDA, ECDC) and international organisations (OECD, UN). Our public health and life sciences portfolio is growing fast, and we are looking for an experienced Healthcare Project Manager to help us deliver it.
THE ROLE
We are looking for a project manager to lead large-scale, complex EU-funded healthcare projects: multi-year, often multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams, high-profile EU clients and demanding delivery standards. You will be accountable for delivery from kick-off to final reporting, including budgets, timelines, teams and client relationships.
Our portfolio includes European guidelines for prostate cancer, evidence-based research prioritisation in the drugs field, GRADE evidence assessments, and quality indicator development following Cochrane standards. You will work closely with our review methodologists, so a good understanding of how systematic reviews and guidelines are developed will help you plan, steer and quality-assure this work as we grow our in-house evidence synthesis capacity.
Day-to-day, you would:

• Lead projects end to end: work planning, timelines, budgets, risk management and quality assurance of deliverables

• Manage several projects and workstreams in parallel, setting priorities and allocating resources across teams

• Act as the main point of contact for EU clients, including inception, interim and final reporting in line with contractual requirements

• Lead multidisciplinary teams of researchers, review methodologists, external experts and consortium partners

• Organise and steer working groups, expert panels and stakeholder consultations

• Oversee the planning and quality of systematic reviews, GRADE assessments, guideline development and quality indicator work, in close collaboration with methodologists

• Drive the use of innovative and AI-assisted review tools in project workflows

• Lead or contribute to tenders and proposals for EU evidence synthesis and health contracts

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Essential:

• PhD in public health, epidemiology, health sciences or a related field

• Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex projects (e.g., multi-year, multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams), ideally EU-funded healthcare or public health projects such as service or framework contracts with the European Commission and its agencies, EU4Health or Horizon Europe

• Experience holding full responsibility for project budgets, timelines, risk management and contractual reporting

• Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing senior client and stakeholder relationships

• Excellent written and spoken English

Strong assets:

• Understanding of how systematic reviews and clinical guidelines are developed (e.g., Cochrane methodology, PRISMA, GRADE, Evidence-to-Decision frameworks)

• Hands-on systematic review experience as an author or review team member

• Experience in cancer evidence review, such as screening, diagnosis, treatment guidelines or HTA

• Track record of writing or leading successful EU tender proposals

• Experience with AI/ML tools in evidence synthesis or health data analysis (e.g., AI-assisted screening, text mining, bibliometrics)

• Publications in cancer, screening, HTA or guideline development

• Familiarity with review and analysis tools (e.g., RevMan, GRADEpro, Covidence, R, Python)

• Experience drafting policy or regulatory documents

CONDITIONS

• Monthly service fee: EUR 4,000-4,500, depending on experience

• Full-time equivalent commitment with flexible working hours

• Remote work within the EU

• Service contract with possibility of extension

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your CV and a short cover letter by 6 November 2026, highlighting your experience managing EU-funded healthcare projects and any relevant work in cancer

About the Role

Reports to the Operations Principal, Change. The Strategic Operations team sits between Product, Technology, and Claims Operations and owns the work that turns a new way of working into one the organization actually runs on.

Not every change at Reserv arrives with a product release behind it. Programs change, client requirements change, and the way a claim is handled changes with them. We are hiring an Operations Lead to own process design and change across claims operations, so that how work is done is written down, current, and changed deliberately.

You own the process side of the function: before-and-after process design for each change, the SOP library and how it is governed, verification that changes landed in practice, and the training and communications for process changes. You will work alongside the Operations Lead who owns product change, since most product releases also change a process, and with claims leadership, who own the work you are documenting. You will be an excellent fit if you have redesigned how an operations team works, can write a process someone will follow, and verify that changes landed in practice.

Duties & Responsibilities

Process Design: Lead the before-and-after process design for each change, product-driven or not, working with leaders, managers, and team leads on what actually shifts in their day. Write the end-to-end process so it can be followed without further explanation, and pressure-test it with the people who will run it before it goes live.

SOP Ownership and Governance: Own the SOP library across lines of business and account variants: its structure, its currency, and its governance. Draft the standard language for each change, drive it into every affected SOP through the SOP owners against a date, and build the auditability that shows who changed what and when. Partner with the Principal on the platform and workflow the library should run on.

Change Readiness for Process Changes: Run process changes against the readiness standard: documented process, approved change plan, training and communications plan, onboarding updated, and metrics defined. Assemble the evidence for sign-off and flag gaps early.

Training, Enablement, and Communications: Build and execute the training and communications for process changes for leaders, managers, and frontline teams, and coordinate with Learning & Development so new-hire onboarding teaches the current process.

Verification and Feedback: Go back after each change and verify it landed in practice, through SOP checks, time studies, and conversations with the teams doing the work. Carry what you find back to the Principal and to claims leadership, and feed it into how the next change is designed.

Metric and Data Management: This person will be responsible for continually tracking metrics to determine success and make data-driven changes to rollouts

title: Langfuse - Senior Backend Engineer (US-East)
description:
WHY BACKEND ENGINEERING AT LANGFUSE

Your work will have an outsized impact.

Langfuse ingests terabytes of AI tracing data per day. When a Fortune 50 company instruments their application with Langfuse, they hit the infrastructure you built. Everything you ship is open source and immediately visible.

The core of your role is making Langfuse fast and affordable at scale: owning the ingestion pipeline, optimizing ClickHouse data models and queries so dashboards load instantly, and building the backend abstractions that let product engineers ship data-heavy features without reinventing the plumbing each time.

You will also make sure Langfuse runs everywhere. You’ll operate Langfuse Cloud across multiple production environments, and make self-hosting effortless. You will support a single Docker Compose setup to enterprise-grade Helm chart deployment.

 

You won’t be solving these problems alone. Langfuse is now part of ClickHouse, which means the people who built the database you’re optimizing are one channel away. Few backend roles give you that kind of access to the internals of your core datastore.

 

YOU WILL GROW AT LANGFUSE BY

- Own and optimize our ingestion pipeline: Langfuse ingests massive volumes of tracing data through a pipeline that flows from our API to ClickHouse. You'll work on throughput, latency, reliability, and cost efficiency at every stage of this pipeline.

- Make ClickHouse fast: our tracing data lives in ClickHouse. You'll design schemas, optimize merge strategies, tune batch inserts, write and review analytical queries that power dashboards and the UI. You'll become an expert on ClickHouse internals - and you'll have the ClickHouse database engineering team one channel away.

- Build new infrastructure-heavy features: things like LLM-as-a-Judge (where we post-process large volumes of ingested data asynchronously), alerting at scale, client-code execution, or batch dataset operations. Build the foundation and, if you like, dip your toes into the frontend for those.

- Test with real data in production: when evaluating a new ClickHouse schema, migration, or query optimization, you'll run load tests against production data to validate that changes actually improve things. We don't guess at performance. We prototype new table designs, run them in parallel on real traffic, and compare before committing.

- Scale for what's next: we're growing fast and new product directions like complex long-running agent observability and real-time evaluation push the infrastructure in new ways. You'll be thinking ahead about what breaks at 10x scale.

 

LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR INFRASTRUCTURE

- From Zero to Scale: Langfuse's Infrastructure Evolution https://langfuse.com/blog/2024-12-langfuse-v3-infrastructure-evolution - deep dive into how we went from Postgres to ClickHouse

- Max talking infrastructure at ClickHouse OpenHouse Amsterdam https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NXYQ5odATrM - recording of our CTO walking through the architecture

- Architecture https://langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Strong backend engineer who gets excited about database internals, query optimization, and distributed systems

- You get excited when working with a ton of data

- Experience with analytical databases, data pipelines, or high-throughput event processing. ClickHouse experience is a big plus but not required

- You organize yourself. You have strong opinions about what to build and how to ship it

- Comfortable reading and writing TypeScript (our backend) and SQL

- Interest in open source software and genuine enjoyment talking to users about their scaling challenges

- Thrives in a small, accountable team where your output is visible and matters

- CS or quantitative degree preferred

 

Bonus points:

 

- Experience with ClickHouse, other OLAP databases, or observability infrastructure

- Former founder

- Background in building data-intensive systems at scale

 

PERKS

The Construction Projects Coordinator plays a key role in advancing CURE International’s mission by helping deliver high-impact hospital construction and renovation projects around the world. This position supports the successful planning, coordination, and execution of projects that directly enable CURE hospitals to provide life-changing surgical care to children.

title: Web Scraping Specialist
description:
Position Overview:
We are seeking a highly skilled Web Scraping Architect to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining web scraping processes to gather data from various online sources efficiently and accurately. As a Web Scraping Specialist, you will play a crucial role in collecting data for competitor analysis, and other business intelligence purposes.
Responsibilities:

• Scalability/Performance: Lead and provide expertise in scraping at scale e-commerce marketplaces.

• Data Source Identification: Identify relevant websites and online sources from which data needs to be scraped. Collaborate with the team to understand data requirements and objectives.

• Web Scraping Design: Develop and implement effective web scraping strategies to extract data from targeted websites. This includes selecting appropriate tools, libraries, or frameworks for the task.

• Data Extraction: Create and maintain web scraping scripts or programs to extract the required data. Ensure the code is optimized, reliable, and can handle changes in the website's structure.

• Data Cleansing and Validation: Cleanse and validate the collected data to eliminate errors, inconsistencies, and duplicates. Ensure data integrity and accuracy throughout the process.

• Monitoring and Maintenance: Continuously monitor and maintain the web scraping processes. Address any issues that arise due to website changes, data format modifications, or anti-scraping mechanisms.

• Scalability and Performance: Optimize web scraping procedures for efficiency and scalability, especially when dealing with a large volume of data or multiple data sources.

• Compliance and Legal Considerations: Stay up-to-date with legal and ethical considerations related to web scraping, including website terms of service, copyright, and privacy regulations.

• Documentation: Maintain detailed documentation of web scraping processes, data sources, and methodologies. Create clear and concise instructions for others to follow.

• Collaboration: Collaborate with other teams such as data analysts, developers, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements and deliver insights effectively.

• Security: Implement security measures to ensure the confidentiality and protection of sensitive data throughout the scraping process.

Requirements:

• Proven experience of 4+ years as a Web Scraping Specialist or similar role, with a track record of successful web scraping projects.

• Expertise in handling dynamic content, user-agent rotation, bypass CAPTCHAs, rate limits, and utilization of proxy services.

• Knowledge on browser fingerprinting

• Has leadership experience.

• Proficiency in programming languages commonly used for web scraping, such as Python, BeautifulSoup, Scrapy, or Selenium.

• Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS, XPath, and other web technologies relevant to web scraping and Coding.

• Knowledge and experience in best of class data storage and retrieval of large volume of scraped data.

• Understanding of web scraping best practices, including handling dynamic content, user-agent rotation, and IP address management.

• Attention to detail and the ability to handle and process large volumes of data accurately.

• Familiarity with data cleansing techniques and data validation processes.

• Good communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Knowledge of web scraping ethics, legal considerations, and compliance with website terms of service.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing web environments

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, or related fields.

• Experience with cloud-based solutions and distributed web scraping systems.

• Familiarity with APIs and data extraction from non-public sources.

• Knowledge of machine learning techniques for data extraction and natural language

description:
The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early!
Citizens Against Government Waste (CAGW) offers a wide variety of opportunities to college students across the country. Unpaid research, communications, and government affairs internships are available on a year-round basis and can vary in length from a semester to a few weeks in duration. Interns can choose to work part-time or full-time, as hours of work are extremely flexible. Our daily work with Capitol Hill and the White House, as well as government agencies and other nonprofit organizations, provides a close and invaluable look at how Washington works. Since CAGW maintains a small staff, interns gain hands-on experience in all aspects of CAGW’s activities. Many projects involve working closely with staff members, while others require a great deal of independence. Interns are considered important members of our staff and actively participate in staff meetings and other events. While interns will also be required to perform clerical duties from time to time, much of the work will be substantive.
Research Internship
Assist in formulating policy papers and collect data for original investigative studies. Research and write for CAGW’s annual publications, which include the Congressional Pig Book, Prime Cuts, Government WasteWatch eNews, and special projects, including issue briefs, and policy papers. Interns will have the opportunity to initiate projects. Research internships are also available in specific areas, including healthcare and science, technology and telecommunications, federal regulations and taxation.

Stand Together Fellowships believes that diversity in experiences, perspectives, knowledge and ideas fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. Our admissions office treats all program participants and applicants with honesty, dignity, respect and sensitivity. We welcome all qualified applicants regardless of color, race, religion, religious creed, sex, gender or gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, ethnicity, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy (including medical needs which may arise from pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), military and veteran status, genetic information, marital or familial status, political affiliation, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances.

title: GM - Relief to Hire
description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

Roo Veterinary is building the modern labor marketplace and operating system for veterinary care. We help hospitals reliably staff shifts and access great veterinary professionals, so care happens when it's needed, without burning out teams.

We're hiring a General Manager to run Relief-to-Hire, the business that turns relief work on Roo into full-time hires. Hospitals book relief veterinarians and technicians on Roo every day, and some of those shifts turn into job offers. Relief-to-Hire makes that a product: hospitals try before they hire and pay a placement fee only when a hire happens. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the management team, you'll own the Relief-to-Hire P&L (placement revenue, contribution margin, and the investment decisions behind them) and be accountable for making Roo the way veterinary practices hire, instead of a job ad or a recruiter.

Relief-to-Hire is an established, growing business: hundreds of hospitals have hired through it, and it has grown every year alongside the relief marketplace it's built on. Until now it has been run by a cross-functional squad rather than a dedicated owner; in January 2027 it becomes its own business unit with a P&L, a budget and a GM. You'll lead a small placement team directly, set priorities for a dedicated product manager and growth analyst, and get much of your leverage from design, engineering, lifecycle marketing and data partners you don't manage. The core of the job: generate hiring intent, use product and automation to turn one-sided interest into mutual interest, and focus people on closing hires.

Key Responsibilities

• Own Relief-to-Hire revenue and contribution margin against plan, and set a plan that beats the business's momentum when the evidence supports it.

• Write the business strategy and the scorecard behind it: the funnel from relief relationships to hand-raises, mutual interest, closed placements and average fee, with one owner per metric.

• Allocate budget and headcount by ROI: invest in product and automation before people, and put people where a human closes the hire.

• Design pricing and terms as one system (placement fee, guarantee, payment plans, enterprise caps and lookbacks) and manage the cash cycle from agreement through invoice and collection.

• Define and own the Relief-to-Hire category with Marketing, so "try before you hire" becomes the default way a practice hires and the term points to Roo.

• Set product priorities for the hiring flow, the recruiter tool and lifecycle campaigns with your product manager and designer; build what only Relief-to-Hire needs and partner with the platform team on shared infrastructure.

• Partner with the Enterprise, Independent Hospitals, Veterinary and Technician GMs on shared supply: agree how placements are credited and what they cost, and make Relief-to-Hire easy for their teams to sell.

• Build and lead the placement team: hire to a high bar, measure and pay on closed hires and cash collected, act on underperformance early, and develop the people who hold hospital relationships.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will:

• Grow placement revenue above plan, with contribution margin inside the guardrail agreed with Finance.

• Grow Relief-to-Hire faster than the relief marke

title: Sr. Manager, Education: e.l.f. Hair & e.l.f. POP
Head of Risk
description:
About the Role:
One owner for the entire risk function at a fintech operating between crypto and traditional payments. You will own enterprise risk end to end, including the risk framework and appetite, DORA and operational resilience, B2B partner risk, fraud risk appetite, capital adequacy, and risk gating for new products.
It is an individual contributor role reporting directly to the CEO, with a seat on the leadership team. You will work daily with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Technology, and the B2B Partnerships team. The foundations are in place (risk register, appetite framework, DORA workstreams). The function needs an owner who proactively surfaces risk, takes a position, and stands behind it.
What You'll Do:
Enterprise Risk & Governance:

• Own the enterprise risk framework: risk register, risk appetite statement, taxonomy, and escalation policy.

• Run the risk reporting cycle: structured updates to the CEO and leadership, plus regulatory risk reporting.

• Chair or co-chair the risk committee: agenda, cadence, participants, and decision authority.

• Build risk ownership across business units.

DORA & Operational Resilience:

• Own the DORA ICT risk framework and lead the Register of Information workstream ahead of the 2027 submission window.

• Own business continuity and disaster recovery planning.

• Own third-party and vendor risk: critical providers, concentration risk, and exit planning.

• Own the PSD2 operational resilience framework, including 4-hour major incident reporting and impact tolerances.

• Partner with the CTO and Head of Security on technology and cloud risk.

EMI & Regulatory Risk:

• Lead the operational risk framework and capital adequacy/safeguarding design for two parallel EMI applications (EU and UK).

• Own ongoing capital adequacy monitoring and escalate breaches.

• Own preparation for risk-focused regulatory examinations and act as the primary contact for risk-related regulator queries.

• Coordinate with Legal on regulatory obligations and with the Chief of Compliance on AML/CTF risk appetite.

B2B Partner & Counterparty Risk:

• Design and own the partner risk assessment framework: onboarding scoring, ongoing due diligence, and risk-tiered monitoring.

• Own risk sign-off on material partnerships, define thresholds for CEO approval, and keep high-risk reviews fast and credible.

• Define which industries, geographies, and business models the company will and will not serve.

• Manage partner concentration risk and delegated-compliance liability as B2B volume scales.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk:

• Build a unified fraud risk framework and appetite across relevant functions, with clear ownership and a single escalation path.

• Set fraud risk appetite by channel, product, and geography, and own decisions when thresholds are breached.

• Coordinate with the Chief of Compliance on the fraud/AML overlap.

• Own the sanctions screening risk framework and escalation policy.

Product & Financial Risk:

• Own product-launch risk gating for new products, markets, and business lines.

• Manage crypto price volatility exposure: conversion timing, settlement risk, and liquidity buffers.

• Own counterparty credit risk: liquidity providers, banking partners, card schemes, and B2B clients.

• Oversee treasury risk: balances, currency exposure, and concentration.

Requirements:

Must have:

• Senior risk leadership (Head of Risk, VP Risk, or equivalent scope) in financial services or fintech within a regulated institution.

• Direct ownership of risk obligations in a licensed fintech, EMI, PSP, payment institution, or crypto company, not advisory or consultancy experience only.

• Hands-on experience with at least one of: DORA ICT risk framework, MiCA capital adequacy and risk requirements, PSD2 operational resilience, or FCA operational resilience.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Provisioning helps organizations of all sizes deploy and manage 1Password through scalable provisioning and organization-management experiences. We build the workflows that help admins onboard people, manage access, and support long-term adoption, with a focus on reliable, secure, and intuitive experiences. As an intern on the team, you’ll work on frontend web experiences in React and TypeScript alongside engineers, product managers, and designers. Our current roadmap includes improving activation, invitation and provisioning-pipeline visibility, error recovery, and other Admin Console workflows.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada/US. This position will be for 4 months - January to April 2027.

What You Can Expect:

- Contribute to frontend features in the 1Password Admin Console using React, TypeScript, CSS, and established design-system patterns.

- Partner with engineers, product managers, and designers to turn customer and admin needs into simple, accessible experiences.

- Write maintainable code, tests, and documentation, and participate in code reviews, debugging, and quality improvements.

- Learn the Provisioning domain and help improve workflows such as onboarding, invitations, user-status visibility, and provisioning error handling.

- Work with the team to investigate problems, communicate progress, and deliver incremental improvements safely.

What we're looking for:

- Confidence: A willingness to take on new challenges, and see them through to completion.

- Humility: You're not afraid to ask "stupid" questions and make mistakes (as long as you learn from them).

- Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

- Teamwork: We work together, and succeed as a team!

- Technical foundations: Working knowledge of React and familiarity with TypeScript and CSS fundamentals.

- Web development foundations: Comfort with HTML, browser behavior, accessibility, Git, and learning established patterns in an existing codebase.

- Project experience: Experience building a small web project through coursework, an internship, personal work, or open source contributions.

Bonus points for:

- Experience with React and TypeScript beyond coursework, including a personal, school, or open source project.

- Familiarity with design systems or component libraries, and with Figma or a similar design tool.

- Exposure to frontend testing tools such as Jest, Testing Library, Playwright, or Cypress.

- Understanding of API integration, asynchronous JavaScript, or backend concepts.

- Interest in security, identity, access management, or building tools for administrators.

title: Data Center Network Operations Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Hiring Locations: Atlanta, GA, Austin, US, Denver, CO, New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Washington DC, US

About the department

In this role, you will be focused on maintaining the Cloudflare global network. You'll work closely with Cloudflare’s SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) team, Network Engineering team, Network Deployment Engineering team and with various vendors and partners (including hardware vendors, datacenter and network providers, and ISPs) to maintain and improve our global infrastructure. You will further be responsible for the development and implementation of consistent processes and visibility measurements for consistent and effective management of our infrastructure. This is a highly visible position that requires deep technical understanding of datacenter infrastructure, networking (physical), and basic experience with data analysis and project management.

To be successful in this position, you should have excellent technical skills, communication skills, and be able to navigate a range of challenges and constraints (e.g. schedule adherence, time zones, and cultures). You will have the opportunity to (literally) build a faster, safer Internet for our millions of users and the billions of web surfers that visit their sites each month.

Who you are

You will thrive in a hypergrowth engineering environment and be self driven with a keen attention to detail. You will come with a deep technical understanding of Data Center colocation environments, network architecture and server technologies. You will be used to working through partners to support infrastructure delivery to a number of remote locations. You will have had experience managing operational environments, and used to developing new approaches to improve delivery efficiency or operational stability.

•
Collaborating with internal teams (Infrastructure, Network Engineering and SRE). Create documentation and manage remote contractors to complete datacenter tasks, working with hardware manufacturers, datacenter and network providers, logistics partners and other service providers in support of our 330+ cities and 125+ countries

•
Maintain Data Center environment operational availability

•
Leverage AI tools to automate repetitive operational tasks, accelerate documentation, and speed up troubleshooting and root-cause analysis

•

The Company
At Nylas, we specialize in making it easier for developers to add email, calendar, and contact management features into their applications. We provide APIs, which streamline the integration of these functionalities, ensuring they are secure and effective. This enables better, safer, and more reliable communication within apps.

description:
About Kennametal
With over 80 years as an industrial technology leader, Kennametal Inc. delivers productivity to customers through materials science, tooling and wear-resistant solutions. Customers across aerospace and defense, earthworks, energy, general engineering and transportation turn to Kennametal to help them manufacture with precision and efficiency. Senior Sales Engineer
The Senior Sales Engineer will operate in the Mining Sector, with specific focus being given to Hard Rock (Underground and Open Cast) Mining customers within the borders of South Africa. The Senior Sales Engineer will be responsible for several activities within the sales process including for the identification of new opportunities at customers known to the business, as well as the identification of new opportunities at new customers. Coupled to this, the Senior Sales Engineer will be responsible for leading commercial negotiations linked to the applicable sales opportunities and with specific focus being given to the attainment of business-related Sales and EBITDA targets.
A key requirement of this role would be to continuously seek to increase Kennametal Market Share within this segment, through the identification of product development opportunities, thereby allowing for the development and introduction of additional products into the segment. The Senior Sales Engineer will be required to be an active participant and key role player in the design / production / engineering / research and development process as the role will be responsible for driving interdepartmental collaboration forward to attain the desired sales related outcomes.
This position will further provide direction and support to both Local Management and the other Sales Engineers within the business to identify additional opportunities and markets. This position will also require long-term planning to accomplish the growth ambitions for this sector.

• Ensure that budgeted margins are maintained.

• Develop and articulate the sales strategy for the role.

• Prepares sales and engineering reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing information.

• Support sales forecasting, plan preparation and sales inventory planning.

• Lead in the design, production, engineering, or research and development process required to ensure that products and services are enhanced to suit the needs of the customer.

• Maintains professional and technical knowledge through various means, including but not limited to the reviewing professional publications and establishing personal networks.

Education

• Technical Engineering Qualification - Preferably in a related field. (Fabrication / Manufacturing / Design of metal components used in the mining or adjacent industries.)
Relevant Work Experience

• 5+ years of sales and sales leadership experience.

• Proven commercial understanding with a track record of developing and executing strategies and action plans.

• Experience in the management of Key Accounts and Distributors specifically within the mining industry.
